_description: AP-01 boundary inventory: every retail Adventure player-count / lead-swap branch in game/src that check_adventure_party_boundaries.py scans for. Each entry is one unique comment-stripped, whitespace-normalized source line (keyed by file+line, counted), so it is stable against line-number drift. The scanner regenerates this set from source and fails closed on any occurrence not listed here (a NEW unclassified branch) or any listed entry whose count no longer matches (a stale entry a later ticket must reclassify or remove).
_scanned_symbols: exact player-count comparison of gNumberOfActivePlayers or gNumActivePlayers against an integer literal (==,!=,>=,<=,>,<)

_treatments.bypass: Retail lead-swap mechanism Adventure Party bypasses rather than generalizes.
_treatments.adapter-seam: Site where a later AP ticket adds a #ifdef NATIVE_PORT party adapter; the core invariant (party never sets the retail 2P globals) is enforced here.
_treatments.inert-by-globals: Retail two-player-adventure branch that is mechanically unreachable in a party session because Adventure Party never sets gIsInTwoPlayerAdventure / gTwoPlayerAdvRace / CHEAT_TWO_PLAYER_ADVENTURE; needs no edit to stay safe.
_treatments.unrelated: Retail menu/load/track-select/results/HUD player-count protocol that Adventure Party does not repurpose; it uses adventure_party_participant_count() and the shared multi-viewport render path instead.

_scope_notes: Assignments to gNumberOfActivePlayers (e.g. the collapse-to-1 at the retail 2P file-entry) and plain getters (return gNumberOfActivePlayers) are not exact-count comparisons and are intentionally out of the scanner's rule scope.
gTwoActivePlayersInAdventure (game/src/objects.c) is a sibling retail flag with the same purpose as gTwoPlayerAdvRace but is not named in the AP-01 scanner rules and is therefore not tracked here.

AP-06 (R15): the party session-creation arm forces the retail 2P flag OFF (literal FALSE, disengage direction only) so a stale gIsInTwoPlayerAdventure from a prior JOINTVENTURE 2P cannot leak into a party session and reach reset_lead_player_index() / the retail-2P consumers. Retail relied on the unconditional else assignment below to clear it; the party arm skips the else, so it disengages itself. Scanner rule 2 permits ONLY this literal-FALSE write in a party adapter; TRUE/nonzero/computed still fail, and a party session never SETS the flag.

1.6.0 online multiplayer: menu_online_versus_race_setup() seeds the Tracks-mode state a direct-boot online race needs without walking any menu (gIsInTracksMode TRUE, gIsInAdventureTwo FALSE, this flag FALSE). It is the online carrier's own retail-flag write inside its NATIVE_PORT arm, not a party adapter; the party session never reaches this function.
